outcome: Sex ratio in favour of males
cohort: The study observed pregnancies that underwent TrophEctoderm (TE) biopsy or exhibited placental PGF downmodulation, comparing their obstetrical and neonatal outcomes to control pregnancies.
finding: The study observed strikingly similar and significantly increased risks of preeclampsia, IUGR, congenital cardiac ventricular septal defects, caesarean section, male sex ratio, and preterm birth in pregnancies following TE biopsy or with placental PGF downmodulation compared to controls, leading to the hypothesis that TE biopsy may induce persistent placental gene dysregulation.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was found to be significantly increased in pregnancies following TE biopsy or with placental PGF downmodulation compared to controls.
